issue_context.title: Saving a layout with an accent in the name shows the wrong character when changing layouts
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2.2 mono stable

**OS/device including version:**
OSX 10.14.6

**Issue description:**
Saving a layout with an accented E in the name makes a layout with a name that's messed up.
Here's what the name should be:
![Capture d’écran, le 2020-07-06 à 15 08 56](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3951049/86654602-ebca6480-bf9a-11ea-8768-6192525dd57f.png)

Here's what the name looks like when I go to Editor -> Editor Layout.
![Capture d’écran, le 2020-07-06 à 15 09 10](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3951049/86654613-ed942800-bf9a-11ea-9a7d-b69cd0cfefc6.png)

**Steps to reproduce:**
Go to Editor -> Editor Layout -> Save Layout
Save a layout with a name that includes an accented character.
Go to Editor -> Editor Layout 
The name will be messed up.
comments:
I can confirm this on commit https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/18c51d3f0c4ddf0bdf347638ca2d781a42de16d2.

It seems the issue stems from the ConfigFile class (which is used to save and load editor layouts). I looked for a bit, don't know how to fix it. The layout name is the section name. Here's an example `editor_layouts.cfg` for reference:

```ini
[façade]

dock_3="Scene,Import"
dock_4="FileSystem"
dock_5="Inspector,Node"
dock_filesystem_split=0
dock_filesystem_display_mode=0
dock_filesystem_file_list_display_mode=1
dock_split_2=0
dock_split_3=0
dock_hsplit_1=0
dock_hsplit_2=70
dock_hsplit_3=-70
dock_hsplit_4=0
```
In my experience this sort of issue is due to different character encoding for saving /loading.

For the record, I tested this on Fedora 31. `file` recognizes `editor_layouts.cfg` as being UTF 8-encoded:

```text
editor_layouts.cfg: UTF-8 Unicode text
```
Most likely the section is parsed by ConfigFile as ascii and not UTF-8.

It looks like ConfigFile defers its parsing to VariantParser. It has one occurrence of `ascii` here, but I'm not sure if it's related: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0fa165f0c936411a775bb41f362da394074b797f/core/variant_parser.cpp#L290

review_comments:
Won't that fail on anything outside of extended ASCII?

CC @bruvzg
I tried it with extended latin and with Japanese characters and it worked, my original solution that is.
With which glyphs does it currently not work?
With `StreamString` it should fail with any character in 0xC0-0xF7 range.
